problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation ${f}^{′}(x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x=0$ that satisfies the condition $f(0)=-1.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution of a Differential Equation With a Given Condition
examples.problem:
Find the particular solution to the differential equation below that satisfies the condition $f(0)=2.$

$$
f'(x) - \dfrac{3}{1+x^2} = 0
$$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation to give

$$
f'(x) = \dfrac{3}{1+x^2}.
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x,$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{3}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\ f(x) & =3\int \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

So our general solution is $f(x) = 3\arctan{x} + C.$ To find a particular solution, we substitute the condition $f(0) = 2$ into our solution and obtain a value for $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =3\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)+C \\ 2 & =3\operatorname{arctan}⁡(0)+C \\ 2 & =0+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is 

$$
f(x)=3\arctan x + 2.
$$

feedback.problem: Which of the following shows some of the solution curves of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{2}(x+2)^{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Integrating the equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{3}{2}(x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\ y & =\frac{3}{2}\int (x+2)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(x+2)^{3}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plot the solution curves by selecting different values for $C.$ The sketch below shows the solution curves for $C=-1,0,1.$
